title: QUIC RFC 9000 Maximum UDP Payload Size Receiver Limit
purpose: Describe the bounded endpoint/runtime path that applies a connection's local max_udp_payload_size transport parameter as a receiver-side UDP payload processing limit.
design_summary: Local transport-parameter commit publishes a QuicConnectionUpdateMaxUdpPayloadSizeEffect carrying either the advertised max_udp_payload_size value or the RFC 9000 default used when the parameter is absent. The endpoint stores that per registered connection and checks already-routed long-header and short-header datagrams before posting a PacketReceived event into the connection runtime. Datagrams whose UDP payload length exceeds the stored local receive limit return a Dropped ingress disposition with no runtime post, and endpoint hosts treat that disposition as terminal local handling rather than as a route miss that should trigger stateless reset or server pre-acceptance policy.
data_and_state_considerations: The receive limit is endpoint-side state keyed by QuicConnectionHandle because it gates datagram dispatch before runtime packet processing. Registered connections start with the default 65527-byte receive limit and are updated by the local transport-parameter effect after TLS publishes local parameters. The endpoint rejects configured limits below QUIC v1's 1200-byte floor.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Datagrams at exactly the local max_udp_payload_size remain eligible for runtime processing.
Datagrams larger than the local max_udp_payload_size are dropped after route attribution and before PacketReceived posting.
Unrouted datagrams and listener pre-acceptance policy remain outside this per-connection receive-limit slice.
The absent transport-parameter case uses the RFC 9000 default max_udp_payload_size value.
risks: This slice proves receiver-side processing suppression for routed datagrams only; it does not claim UDP socket receive-buffer sizing, PMTU discovery, peer send-size enforcement, broader Section 18.2 closure, public configuration APIs, or hosted interop readiness.
No parser, serializer, encoder, or decoder is introduced. Existing transport-parameter codec proof remains separate from this endpoint dispatch proof.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S18P2-0007 by preventing over-limit routed UDP payloads from being posted into the connection runtime.
